agentMessages.text: I’ll build this as a small static data visualization so it can ship with GitHub Pages, using only local bundled data and a lightweight test suite. I’m going to inspect the workspace and tooling first, then create the app, docs, tests, metadata, and publish it.

The repo is empty apart from the run artifacts, and the local Node/GitHub CLI toolchain is ready. I’m going to turn the actual `codex-events.jsonl` from this run into a static “run pulse” visualization, which keeps the data real and avoids external services.

I’ve got the shape now: a dependency-free static site plus a Node parser that converts JSONL events into browser data. I’m going to add the source, tests, docs, and Pages-ready `public/` files in one scoped pass.

The core project files are in place: parser, generator, static UI, tests, README, and docs. Next I’m creating the lockfile, generating the data artifact from the real run log, and running the test suite.
Tests are passing against both synthetic edge cases and the bundled run log. I’m checking the GitHub account/repo target now so the metadata can be written with truthful URLs before the first commit.

The GitHub owner is `jamiegonzalez929`, so I can now fill the project metadata and Pages URL deterministically. I’m adding a GitHub Pages workflow that deploys the generated `public/` directory rather than moving documentation around to fit branch-based Pages constraints.

Metadata and deployment wiring are added. I’m going to regenerate the data once more, rerun tests, and do a quick local HTTP check so the static app is verified through the same serving path people will use.

Port `4173` is already occupied on this machine, so I’m replacing the fixed Python server script with a small Node static server that automatically tries the next port. That keeps the documented run command accurate even when the default port is busy.

The local HTTP smoke test passed and I stopped the server. I noticed the README still mentioned the old Python server, so I’m tightening that documentation before the final data generation and commit.
Final local tests are green. I’m committing the finished repository now, then I’ll create the public GitHub repo, push `main`, and enable Pages for the Actions workflow.

The repository is created and `main` is pushed. I’m enabling GitHub Pages in Actions mode now, then I’ll check the deployment workflow status and update anything if GitHub reports a configuration issue.
Pages deployed successfully. I’m doing one final remote check against the GitHub Pages URL and repository state before closing out.

The Pages check passed, but the live `codex-events.jsonl` kept changing after the commit because this conversation is still being logged. I’m adjusting the repo so the volatile live run artifacts are not tracked while the generated static dataset remains bundled and tested.

I removed the volatile live log from tracking and kept the generated site data in the repo. To make `npm run build:data` runnable after clone, I’m adding a fixed snapshot copy under `data/` and making the builder fall back to that when a live log is not present.
